messages:
maria: Noticing higher CPU on host-proxy after yesterday's kernel packing change. Small streaming requests (<=128 tokens) have P95 up ~25ms; flamegraphs point to many tiny writev/syscall bursts.

jin: I reproduced on staging. The kernel mapper now colocates multiple model variants on the same worker which sounds great for throughput but increases write churn for multiplexed streams. Each stream currently flushes ~4x more often.

bench-bot: Synthetic repro: `wrk -c80 -t6 -d45s stream_small.lua` 
result: avg writev calls/request: 6.8 -> baseline 1.9.

tom: Attached a sampled trace: `https://perf.example/runs/5101/trace.html` 1:00: tokenization -> unicode_normalize -> memcpy -> writev -> epoll_wait. The unicode_normalize pass is new in our latest tokenizer refactor.

maria: Hmm. Two orthogonal issues: 1) kernel packing increasing multiplexing across KV shards -> more cache misses/evictions; 2) tokenizer extra normalization copy path. Which to attack first?

jin: Low-risk config first: bias batcher to preserve KV affinity. I added `runtime.batch_policy = "kv_affinity"` and ran a quick canary. KV hit-rate rose 3.4% and writev calls/request dropped to 3.2, p95 improved ~12ms. Patch: `config: add batch_policy option (defaults to throughput)`

maria: Good. Can we also do host-side write coalescing as a safety net so we don't rely solely on batch mapping? Coalesce window of 5ms or up to 16KB before grpc write.

tom: I implemented a prototype in the proxy: accumulate outgoing chunks per-stream leader and issue a single writev if either size>16KB or time>5ms. Local bench: writev calls/request down to 1.6 and p95 ~20ms better than baseline. However, it adds 3-4ms median for very tiny streams.

jin: Tradeoff is acceptable for most product traffic (median unchanged or +2ms), but P95 improves. We should guard with feature flag `proxy.coalesce_small_writes=true` and experiment.

ops-bot: Canary start: batch-policy-kv-affinity + proxy-coalesce flag -> cluster canary 510101A (monitoring: /dash/host/streaming)

maria: Also filed a follow-up perf task to remove the normalization memcpy in tokenizer: ticket INF-9832. Tom, can you add a microbenchmark that asserts tokenizer does <=1 extra memcpy per 1k tokens?

tom: Yep, I'll land `eng/runtime/bench/tokenize_memcpy_test.go` that fuzzes random UTF8 inputs and checks syscall counts via a lightweight shim.

jin: Observed an interesting side-effect: when kernel selector packs more models per worker, eviction storms shift to a small set of shards. We should surface per-worker eviction spikes in the dashboard and alert on >2% delta. I'll add metrics `kvcache.evictions_per_worker` and `kvcache.hit_rate_by_worker`.

maria: Plan recap: (1) enable batch_policy kv_affinity in canary, (2) enable proxy.coalesce_small_writes flag in canary, (3) monitor KV per-worker metrics + writev counts, (4) run tokenizer memcpy micro-optim and benchmark. If canary looks good after 30m, roll to 25% and run 2h observability window.

bench-bot: Preliminary canary numbers (10m): p95 latency -14ms, host CPU -4.6%, kv hit_rate +2.9%. writev calls/request 1.7.

maria: Those look promising. Jin, can you keep an eye on subtler regressions (tail latencies on larger streams)?

jin: Watching. Also adding a fallback into kernel-selector: if enabling a mapped kernel leads to >3% drop in kv hit-rate within 5min, mark kernel mapping as "deprioritize" for small_streams. I'll prototype selector scoring that includes kv_affinity_score and observed_kv_delta.

maria: Thanks. If everything stays green, we'll include notes in release that the change reduces host churn for small streaming workloads and adds a coalescing proxy flag. Also mention tokenizer memcpy removal planned.

ops-bot: Canary roll complete: 510101A -> 25% rollout. Follow monitoring link: /dash/host/streaming?canary=510101A

maria: Great work team. Let's keep this thread for observations during the 2h window; if any spikes appear tag oncall and we may rollback.

jin: FYI I'll open a short doc describing selector scoring change: includes kv_affinity, model_variant_cardinality, and latency_impact_estimate.

maria: Closing triage for now. Will post a short postmortem if we need a revert. :rocket:
